name: Vladislav Tretiak
milestone_by_age_26: Became starting goaltender for the Soviet national team and won the 1970 World Ice Hockey Championship at age 18, followed by Olympic gold in 1972 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Tretiak entered the CSKA Moscow hockey school at age 11 and was practicing with the Central Red Army club by 15. He joined the CSKA Moscow roster at 17 in 1969 and became the Soviet national team's starting goaltender in 1970, winning the World Championship that year. By age 26 he had won three Olympic golds and multiple World Championships.
family_context_summary: Father served 37 years as a military pilot; mother was a physical education teacher. Family was from Dmitrovsky District in the USSR.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother's physical education background provided some athletic orientation, but no direct hockey domain expertise in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CSKA Moscow pipeline,Soviet national team system,early specialization,physical talent
evidence_summary: Tretiak entered the CSKA Moscow children's hockey school at age 11, joined the senior CSKA Moscow roster at 17, and became the Soviet national team starting goaltender at 18. The CSKA/Red Army system was the elite Soviet sports pipeline, concentrating the best talent and resources. His father was a military pilot and mother a PE teacher, providing a modest but athletically oriented family background. He won the World Championship in 1970 and Olympic gold in 1972, both before age 26.
starting_point: Born to a military pilot father and physical education teacher mother in Dmitrovsky District, USSR; modest Soviet family with athletic orientation.
current_position: President of the Ice Hockey Federation of Russia; widely regarded as one of the greatest goaltenders in hockey history; inducted into Hockey Hall of Fame in 1989 and IIHF Hall of Fame in 1997.

name: Marijan Beneš
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Amateur Boxing Championship gold medal in the light welterweight category at Belgrade in 1973 at age 22, and was named Best Athlete of Yugoslavia that year.
early_history_summary: Beneš started boxing at age 10 at Sloboda Tuzla, allegedly defeating an 18-year-old in his first ring appearance. At 16 he transferred to BK Slavija in Banja Luka, where he spent his entire amateur career. He won nine Bosnia titles and four Yugoslav championships before claiming the European amateur title in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born to a Croat father Josip, a music teacher, and Serb mother Marija. Grew up in Tuzla with three brothers and one sister; the Beneš brothers were known as athletes competing for Sloboda Tuzla.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a music teacher, not directly related to boxing. However, the family environment supported competitive athletics, with all four Beneš brothers competing in boxing for Sloboda Tuzla.

evidence_summary: Beneš began boxing at age 10 at Sloboda Tuzla and transferred to BK Slavija Banja Luka at 16, where he developed through the Yugoslav amateur boxing system. He accumulated extensive reps with nine Bosnia titles and four Yugoslav championships before winning the European Amateur Championship in 1973 at age 22. His father was a music teacher and the family supported athletic competition among the four Beneš brothers. Coaches Bego Huseljić and Miloš Todorović provided early guidance.
starting_point: Born in Belgrade to a Croat music teacher father and Serb mother; grew up in Tuzla in a modest Yugoslav family with four siblings who all competed in boxing.
current_position: Died on 4 September 2018 at age 67 in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina; final role: retired boxer, later named best Bosnian boxer of the 20th century in 2020.

name: Bret Hart
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Stampede International Tag Team Championship with brother Keith in 1978 at age 21, and went on to win multiple Stampede Wrestling titles including the North American Heavyweight Championship before age 26.
early_history_summary: Hart grew up in the Hart wrestling family in Calgary, training in his father Stu Hart's Dungeon from age 9. He won the Calgary city amateur wrestling championship in 1974 and a collegiate title at Mount Royal College in 1977. He joined Stampede Wrestling as a referee in 1976 and made his in-ring debut in 1978, quickly winning tag team and singles titles.
family_context_summary: Eighth child of wrestling patriarch Stu Hart and wife Helen; grew up in the Hart family mansion in Calgary with eleven siblings. Father owned and operated Stampede Wrestling promotion and trained wrestlers in the household basement known as the Dungeon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Stu Hart was a professional wrestler, wrestling promoter, and trainer who owned Stampede Wrestling. Bret grew up immersed in the wrestling business, witnessing training sessions in the Dungeon from childhood and distributing fliers for shows as a young boy.

evidence_summary: Bret Hart was born into the Hart wrestling family, with father Stu Hart owning Stampede Wrestling and training wrestlers in the household Dungeon. Bret began amateur wrestling at age 9, won city and collegiate championships, then transitioned to pro wrestling in his father's promotion. He won his first Stampede tag team title at 21 in 1978 and accumulated multiple championships by age 26. The family-domain advantage was exceptionally strong: his father's promotion, training facility, and wrestler network all directly catalyzed his early career.

He debuted professionally in 1983 and began his first major serial, Pineapple Army, in 1985, followed by Yawara! in 1986.

name: Jean Nouvel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Nouvel obtained his architecture degree in 1971 at age 26 and started a practice, but his first internationally recognized building (Institut du Monde Arabe) came in 1981 at age 36.
early_history_summary: Nouvel studied at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, winning first prize in the national entrance exam at age 20. He worked as assistant to Claude Parent and Paul Virilio from 1967 to 1970, becoming a project manager for a large apartment complex. He started his own practice with François Seigneur in 1970 and co-founded the Mars 1976 movement, but did not complete a major building until the 1980s.

family_context_summary: Born in Havlíčkův Brod, Czechoslovakia. Brother Jaroslav Holík also played for Dukla Jihlava and the Czechoslovak national team, sharing the 1972 world title and Olympic medals. Nephew Bobby Holík played in the NHL for two decades.
parent_family_domain_summary: Brother Jaroslav was a teammate at Dukla Jihlava and on the national team, providing a high-trust sibling collaborator in the same sport. The Holík family produced multiple generations of hockey players.

He debuted at the Olympics at age 19 in 1964, winning bronze, and accumulated multiple World Championship and Olympic medals before age 26. His brother Jaroslav was a teammate on both Dukla Jihlava and the national team, providing a strong sibling collaborator. name: Florin Gheorghiu
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Junior Chess Championship in 1963 at age 19 and became an International Master the same year; earned the Grandmaster title in 1965 at age 21, becoming Romania's first Grandmaster.
early_history_summary: Gheorghiu was born in Ploiești, Romania during World War II. His chess talent was evident early; he won the Romanian Championship for the first time in 1960 at age 16. He became World Junior Champion and International Master in 1963 at 19, and Romania's first Grandmaster in 1965 at 21. He won the Romanian Championship nine times and represented Romania in every Chess Olympiad from 1962 to 1990.
